title: BMA executor bma-file types
description: fs.mount and fs.unmount (machine-scoped executors with the fs capability). bma-file HTTP routes live under the service_url the harness sends (a complete prefix ending in /v1/machines/{machine_id}/fs, for example https://executor.example.com/v1/machines/mach_01/fs, operations at <service_url>/<op>; the executor does not compose the machine id); they are authenticated with the mount token, not executor methods.

FsMount.description: One view to mount. path is the absolute mount point on the executor host (derived from session_files by the harness; the skills view is at <root>/<agent_session_id>/skills for an executor that declared fs.skills_per_session and a root, otherwise /mnt/skills). Mount points of different sessions never overlap, and the executor mounts exactly the path it is given. readonly is also fixed inside token; the executor mounts read-only when it is true. token is a capability token for this session and machine: keep it in memory only, never write it to disk, argv, environment or logs.

view.description: uploads, skills. Open enum: outputs and memory follow.

options.description: Reserved mount tuning (string values); unknown keys are ignored.

FsMountResult.description: fs.mount result. state is "mounted" once every listed view is mounted and serving, or "failed" with error_code and error (nothing stays half-mounted).

FsUnmountResult.description: fs.unmount result. pending_bytes is data not yet committed to bma-file when flush was requested (always 0 for read-only views).
